sysd-scale-061.caption: Compare what each direction of growth adds, gains and costs.
rows: Simple, easier to manage, data consistent
High downtime, harder to upgrade, single point of failure

sysd-scale-136.caption: Speeding up the part that takes most time gives the bigger overall gain.
bars: Speed up the 3 s part twice
Speed up the 1 s part five times

sysd-q-067.caption: A metric crossing its threshold sets off a chain that ends in a cooldown.
sysd-q-067.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A[Metric crosses a threshold] --> B[Scaling policy changes desired capacity]
B --> C[Group launches or removes instances]
C --> D[Cooldown blocks further scaling]

sysd-scale-069.caption: Each added nine cuts the yearly downtime budget sharply.

sysd-scale-074.caption: The same two 99.9% components give a lower or a higher total depending on layout.
rows: Product of availabilities, so it decreases
1 minus product of unavailabilities, so it increases

sysd-scale-047.caption: Waiting for the remote copy buys safety and costs speed.
rows: Local and remote storage both acknowledge

sysd-scale-049.caption: Writes go to the primary, which replicates them to the replicas that serve reads.
sysd-scale-049.mermaid:
flowchart TD
W[Inserts, deletes, updates] -->|sent to| P[(Primary database)]
P -->|replicates to| R[(Read replicas)]
R -->|serve| Q[Reads, such as order history]

sysd-scale-126.caption: The two kinds of CRDT trade bandwidth against what the network must guarantee.
rows: Middleware that never drops or duplicates
Whole state must reach every replica
Less bandwidth when transactions are few

sysd-scale-123.caption: Follow the arrows from lost heartbeat links to two data sets that disagree.
sysd-scale-123.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A[Heartbeat links fail] --> B[Each node thinks it is alone]
B --> C[Each side serves clients separately]
C --> D[Data corrupted or inconsistent]
